biography.plain_text: Jean-Jacques Laurent is a French industrialist from Vendée and the former head of PRB. He expanded the specialist building materials company founded by his father, Jacques, in 1975, developing its range of coatings, adhesives and insulation products. The family sold PRB to Holcim in 2022, ending decades of independent ownership.

long_biography.plain_text:
During an economic downturn, Jean-Jacques Laurent expanded capacity at PRB, the building materials manufacturer he led, to prepare for the recovery. The programme added nine logistics platforms and factories for tile adhesive and polystyrene insulation. It also broadened the company’s product offering beyond the façade coatings on which its reputation rested.

With his daughter, Cécilia Segarra, Laurent co-founded Solarem, joining Denis Grit’s solar lighting project. Grit had begun developing lights for rural school bus stops, where children could be left waiting in darkness. Laurent brought his industrial experience to developing outdoor lighting that could be installed without trenches or connection to the electricity grid.
long_biography.html:
During an economic downturn, Jean-Jacques Laurent expanded capacity at PRB, the building materials manufacturer he led, to prepare for the recovery. The programme added nine logistics platforms and factories for tile adhesive and polystyrene insulation. It also broadened the company’s product offering beyond the façade coatings on which its reputation rested.

With his daughter, Cécilia Segarra, Laurent co-founded Solarem, joining Denis Grit’s solar lighting project. Grit had begun developing lights for rural school bus stops, where children could be left waiting in darkness. Laurent brought his industrial experience to developing outdoor lighting that could be installed without trenches or connection to the electricity grid.
